content: Wheat is best planted in early autumn (October–November) in temperate climates. Sow seeds 2–3 cm deep in well-drained loamy soil with pH 6.0–7.5. Ensure adequate moisture at sowing.
Apply 120 kg/ha nitrogen split into three doses: at sowing, tillering, and heading. Phosphorus at 60 kg/ha and potassium at 40 kg/ha at sowing improve yields significantly.
Maize requires 150–200 kg/ha nitrogen. Apply one-third at planting and two-thirds as side-dress at knee-high stage. DAP at 100 kg/ha provides phosphorus needs.
Maize is most sensitive to water stress during tasseling and silking. Provide 25 mm water per week. Drip irrigation is 40% more efficient than flood irrigation for maize.
Transplant rice seedlings at 20–25 days old. Spacing of 20×15 cm optimizes yield. Puddled fields maintain standing water of 2–5 cm during vegetative stage.
Stem borers are major rice pests. Use pheromone traps, remove stubble after harvest, and apply Trichogramma egg parasitoids. Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides to protect natural enemies.
Late blight (Phytophthora infestans) causes brown lesions on leaves and tubers. Apply copper-based fungicides preventively. Resistant varieties like Kufri Jyoti reduce dependence on chemicals.
Store potatoes at 4°C with 90–95% humidity. Cure tubers at 15°C for 10 days post-harvest to heal wounds. Avoid light exposure to prevent greening (solanine buildup).
Tomatoes need 25–30 mm water per week. Drip irrigation with mulching reduces evaporation by 35%. Avoid overhead watering to reduce foliar diseases like early blight.
Indeterminate tomato varieties benefit from removing suckers below the first flower cluster. This improves air circulation and redirects energy to fruit development.
Coffee leaf rust (Hemileia vastatrix) appears as orange powdery spots on leaf undersides. Apply copper hydroxide at 3 kg/ha. Shade-grown coffee shows 30% less rust incidence.
Harvest coffee cherries when 80% are deep red. Selective picking improves cup quality. Process within 24 hours: wet processing yields cleaner flavors than dry method.
Maintain soil organic matter above 3% through crop residue retention and green manuring. Rotate legumes to fix nitrogen naturally. Test soil every 2 years for pH and nutrients.
Compost should maintain C:N ratio of 25–30:1. Turn pile every 2 weeks. Mature compost is dark, crumbly, and earthy-smelling. Apply 5–10 tons/ha to improve soil structure.
Drip irrigation delivers water directly to root zones, saving 30–50% water compared to furrow. Maintain system pressure at 1–1.5 bar. Flush lines monthly to prevent clogging.
Integrated Pest Management combines cultural, biological, and chemical controls. Scout fields weekly, use economic thresholds, prioritize biocontrol agents, and use pesticides as last resort.
Organic certification requires 3-year transition. Use neem-based biopesticides, vermicompost, and crop rotation. Premiums of 20–40% justify higher labor costs for smallholders.
Climate-smart agriculture includes drought-tolerant varieties, conservation tillage, and agroforestry. Diversify crops to spread risk. Use weather-indexed insurance where available.
